candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments and Settlement Systems Statistics (PSS) dataset
candidates.why_relevant: Master payments-statistics dataset of the ECB (ex-SDW). Slovenia (SI) appears as a country row for payment instruments, volumes/values, terminals, cards, and infrastructures under the harmonised ECB/2020/59 payments statistics regulation. This is the single most comparable machine-readable source for SI payment statistics.
candidates.legal_status: ECB open data / re-use permitted with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX 2.1 REST API at https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service/data/PSS/... with CSV response; filter REF_AREA=SI; schedule semi-annual pulls (end-Jan and end-Jul)
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + ECB Data Portal dataset navigation
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Slovenia cards ATM POS dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — ATM, OTC and POS terminal transactions (PTT) dataset
candidates.why_relevant: The most granular EU-comparable series for ATM and POS terminal counts and transactions, with Slovenia available at annual and half-yearly frequency. Directly answers ATM/POS installed-base and throughput questions for the SI market.
candidates.legal_status: ECB open data / re-use permitted with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX API series query on the PTT dataflow filtered to REF_AREA=SI; CSV export; compare against Banka Slovenije national release
candidates.discovered_via_method: search result snowball from ECB Data Portal payments category
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Slovenia cards ATM POS dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Card payments and cash withdrawals using cards (PCP), incl. fraud data
candidates.why_relevant: Card transaction volumes/values and card-fraud series by country, including Slovenia; underpins card-penetration and card-fraud-rate benchmarking against euro area peers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Navigate the payment-statistics data category to resolve the exact dataflow code, then SDMX API pull filtered to SI
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Slovenia cards ATM POS dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Slovenia country landing page
candidates.why_relevant: Single entry point enumerating every ECB dataset in which Slovenia appears as a reference area; excellent snowballing hub for discovering additional SI-relevant dataflows beyond payments (MFI, banknotes, interest rates).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the page to enumerate dataflow codes; feed into an SDMX catalogue
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Slovenia cards ATM POS dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — SDMX 2.1 web service / bulk download documentation
candidates.why_relevant: Defines the machine access path (base URL https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service, CSV/SDMX-JSON/XML, dataflow discovery, bulk download). Essential engineering documentation for automating every ECB series in this cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Read once to build a generic SDMX client; re-check annually for API changes
queries_used: ECB Data Portal SDMX 2.1 API documentation bulk download dataflow

candidates.source_name: ECB payments statistics press releases (semi-annual, e.g. first half of 2025)
candidates.why_relevant: Narrative + tables accompanying each semi-annual payments-statistics release; gives release calendar, revisions notes and headline euro-area context in which the SI row must be read.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the paysec press section twice a year (end-Jan, end-Jul); archive HTML + linked annex tables
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Slovenia cards ATM POS dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB SPACE — Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (hub)
candidates.why_relevant: The definitive cash-usage-at-POS evidence base, run since 2016 (2016/2019/2022/2024 waves) with country-level results. Slovenia is repeatedly among the highest cash-share countries (64% of POS payments by number in 2024), which is decisive context for cash-handling, ATM and POS strategy. No national equivalent exists.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch main report PDF plus statistical annexes on each wave (roughly every 2-3 years); extract SI country rows into a longitudinal table
queries_used: ECB SPACE study 2024 cash usage payment attitudes euro area Slovenia

candidates.source_name: ECB SPACE 2024 statistical annexes (Annex A/B country tables)
candidates.why_relevant: Country-by-country breakdowns (payment shares by instrument, value bands, P2P, online, cash access/acceptance perceptions) where the Slovenia column lives. This is the extractable layer, not the narrative report.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: PDF table extraction (per-wave, one-off) into a normalised country/indicator/year table
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from SPACE hub search results
queries_used: ECB SPACE study 2024 cash usage payment attitudes euro area Slovenia

candidates.source_name: ECB — Use of cash by companies in the euro area (SUCH / company cash survey)
candidates.why_relevant: Merchant/company-side counterpart to SPACE (waves 2021, 2024, 2026): cash acceptance rates, deposit/withdrawal behaviour, payment-method acceptance criteria. Directly relevant to POS acceptance and cash-handling demand in Slovenia; euro-area cash acceptance fell 96%->88% between 2021 and 2024.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch each wave's report page/PDF; extract SI-specific figures where the country breakdown is published
queries_used: ECB Study on the use of cash by companies SUCH euro area 2022 report

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Banknotes statistics (BKN)
candidates.why_relevant: Monthly national-issuance (net) series of euro banknotes and coins per NCB, plus semi-annual cash-logistics data — an objective, high-frequency proxy for cash demand in Slovenia to triangulate with SPACE survey cash shares.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX API on BKN dataflow, key pattern BKN.M.SI.*; monthly pull around the 12th working day
candidates.discovered_via_method: targeted search on ECB banknote circulation series
queries_used: ECB banknotes circulation statistics data portal BKN currency series euro area

candidates.source_name: ECB — Payments statistics indicators (key figures dashboard)
candidates.why_relevant: Curated headline indicator set (per-capita card payments, terminal counts, instrument mix) that is quickest for cross-country benchmarking of Slovenia without building SDMX keys.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/periodic review; resolve underlying series keys and automate via SDMX
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Slovenia cards ATM POS dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB — Payments statistics methodology / data-category notes
candidates.why_relevant: Defines concepts, reporting population, frequency (semi-annual, with quarterly high-level and card indicators) and publication lag (H1 by end-Jan, H2 by end-Jul). Needed to avoid mis-comparing SI figures across regimes and to time collection.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off read, re-check on regulation amendments
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payments statistics Slovenia cards ATM POS dataset

candidates.source_name: EBA–ECB Joint Report on Payment Fraud (annual series)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual EU/EEA fraud dataset under PSD2 with country-level breakdowns by instrument (cards, credit transfers, direct debits, cash withdrawals, e-money) and SCA vs non-SCA splits. Gives Slovenia a comparative fraud-risk position; 2024 EEA card losses EUR 1.329bn (+29% YoY).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF fetch (Aug 2024 and Dec 2025 editions observed); extract SI rows from country annex tables
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query on EBA + snowball to ECB press release
queries_used: ECB EBA 2024 report payment fraud PSD2 data country breakdown card fraud

candidates.source_name: EBA Payment Institutions Register (PIR, PSD2 central register)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative EU-wide register of authorised payment institutions, e-money institutions, PISPs, AISPs and their agents, filterable by country of establishment — the cleanest way to enumerate and track the Slovenian non-bank PSP population over time. Whole register is downloadable.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic (monthly/quarterly) bulk download of the register file, filter home member state = SI, diff snapshots to detect entries/exits and passporting changes
queries_used: EBA payment institutions register e-money Slovenia PSD2 credit institutions register EUCLID

candidates.source_name: EBA Credit Institutions Register (CIR) and other lists of institutions (EUCLID)
candidates.why_relevant: Master data on credit institutions and other supervised entities across the EU, sourced from EUCLID; gives the authoritative, comparable list of Slovenian banks/branches underlying any market-structure or bank-count analysis.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly download; filter country=SI; reconcile with Banka Slovenije national list and ECB MFI list
queries_used: EBA payment institutions register e-money Slovenia PSD2 credit institutions register EUCLID

candidates.source_name: European Commission (DG FISMA) — Payment services policy hub
candidates.why_relevant: Central pointer to PSD2/PSD3-PSR, Instant Payments Regulation, digital euro legislative files, impact assessments and consultation responses — the regulatory drivers that reshape the Slovenian payments market and often carry country-level annexes/studies.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the hub and linked consultations/studies; capture commissioned studies with member-state annexes
queries_used: European Commission instant payments regulation report digital euro retail payments strategy 2025

candidates.source_name: European Court of Auditors — Special Report 01/2025 'Digital payments in the EU'
candidates.why_relevant: Independent audit of EU digital-payments policy; audits typically expose data gaps, supervisory weaknesses and member-state comparisons that are not visible in ECB statistics, and cite underlying datasets useful for snowballing.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off PDF fetch; mine footnotes for further datasets; monitor ECA publications feed
queries_used: European Commission instant payments regulation report digital euro retail payments strategy 2025

candidates.source_name: ECB Euro Retail Payments Board (ERPB) — statements and instant-payments reporting
candidates.why_relevant: ERPB statements track SCT Inst reachability/adoption and market-side deliverables; a leading indicator of instant-payment rollout affecting Slovenian banks ahead of statistical confirmation in PSS.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Watch meeting pages twice yearly; download statements/annexes
queries_used: European Commission instant payments regulation report digital euro retail payments strategy 2025

candidates.source_name: ECB Retail Payments Strategy hub
candidates.why_relevant: Frames ECB's own priorities (pan-European solutions, digital euro, instant payments) and links to the reports and oversight frameworks that determine what statistics get published next.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly review for new linked publications
queries_used: European Commission instant payments regulation report digital euro retail payments strategy 2025

candidates.source_name: Eurostat — ICT usage / e-banking and e-commerce datasets (isoc_bde15cbc, isoc_i, isoc_e)
candidates.why_relevant: EU-harmonised household/enterprise survey data on internet banking, online purchasing and enterprise web sales with Slovenia as a country row; the standard demand-side complement to ECB payment counts (e.g. SI web-sales share of turnover 4.63%).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Eurostat SDMX/JSON API (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination) pull filtered geo=SI; annual refresh after December releases
queries_used: Eurostat isoc_ec internet banking e-commerce Slovenia data.europa.eu dataset

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije coverage of ECB studies (Slovenian-language gateway to SPACE)
candidates.why_relevant: The NCB's Slovenian-language write-up of the ECB SPACE results is the only place euro-area cash-study findings are rendered with explicit Slovenian framing and local terminology; it is also the practical entry point for sl-language discovery of ECB material (ECB itself publishes SPACE/PSS almost exclusively in English).
candidates.source_subtype: NCB press release relaying supranational study

candidates.why_relevant: Documents the national implementation of ECB Regulation ECB/2020/59 — which SI institutions report, on what templates and deadlines. Explains the provenance, granularity and lag of the SI rows that appear in ECB PSS/PTT, and names reporting-agent categories for actor mapping.

negative_findings.description: ECB SPACE, SUCH and the PSS/PTT statistical datasets appear to be published only in English; no Slovenian-language version of the SPACE report, its annexes, or the ECB Data Portal payment datasets was found in sl-language searching.
negative_findings.result_summary: Slovenian-language queries returned only Banka Slovenije relays and national media coverage (24ur, RTV SLO, Žurnal24) of the ECB findings, not ECB-hosted sl content.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection pipelines for this cell must be English-language; sl-language monitoring has to be pointed at bsi.si rather than ecb.europa.eu, and any sl glossary must be built from NCB wording.

negative_findings.description: No machine-readable, per-country microdata or downloadable dataset for SPACE or the company cash survey (SUCH) was located — only PDF reports and PDF annexes.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced report HTML/PDF and annex PDFs; no CSV/SDMX distribution of SPACE country results was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cash-usage evidence for Slovenia must be extracted from PDF tables each wave rather than pulled from an API; budget for table extraction and expect 2-3 year refresh cadence.

negative_findings.description: The legacy ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (sdw.ecb.europa.eu) referenced in the seed brief has been superseded by the ECB Data Portal (data.ecb.europa.eu) with a new API host (data-api.ecb.europa.eu).
negative_findings.result_summary: All current documentation and dataset pages found resolve to data.ecb.europa.eu; no live SDW-branded payments page was surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any stored SDW URLs or SDW API endpoints in existing collection code are likely stale and should be migrated; unverified whether old links still redirect.

negative_findings.description: No page in this cell was actually fetched end-to-end during this pass; all URLs come from search-result metadata and snippets.
negative_findings.result_summary: Discovery was search-driven; liveness, exact dataflow keys (e.g. the PCP dataset code) and annex file names remain unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream deterministic verification must confirm URLs and resolve exact SDMX dataflow/series keys before any scheduled collection is built.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query https://data-api.ecb.europa.eu/service/dataflow and the relevant DSDs, then build and store SI series keys for each indicator of interest.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up sweep on ecb.europa.eu/paym oversight pages, EPC SCT Inst reachability statistics, and digital-euro progress reports for SI-relevant content.

coverage_gaps.description: EU open-data catalogue (data.europa.eu) was not searched directly as an aggregator index for SI payments/banking datasets.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search data.europa.eu for 'payments', 'cards', 'ATM', 'Slovenia' to find re-published or derived datasets and their APIs.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovenian-language coverage in this cell is structurally thin because supranational aggregators publish in English; only NCB relays provided sl terms.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the sl glossary (statistika plačil, plačilni instrumenti, bankomat, POS terminal, gotovina, plačilne navade, plačilna institucija, institucija za izdajo elektronskega denarja) from bsi.si and reuse it in the national-source cells.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Read the ECB payments-statistics methodology page and note pre/post-2022 comparability caveats before building SI time series.

brief: For Slovenia, the EU/ECB layer is the strongest and most automatable part of the payments evidence base: the ECB Data Portal (successor to the SDW) carries SI as a country row in the PSS, PTT, PCP and BKN dataflows, all reachable through a documented SDMX 2.1 REST API at data-api.ecb.europa.eu with semi-annual publication (H1 by end-January, H2 by end-July). On cash, the ECB SPACE consumer study and the companion company cash survey (SUCH) are the only rigorous, cross-country measurements of cash use at the point of sale — Slovenia consistently ranks near the top of the euro area (64% of POS payments by number in the 2024 wave) — but both are PDF-only, so extraction rather than API access is required. Regulatory and structural sources complete the cell: the EBA PSD2 Payment Institutions Register and Credit Institutions Register give a downloadable, diffable population of Slovenian PSPs and banks, the annual EBA–ECB payment fraud report gives country-level fraud benchmarks, and the Commission/ERPB/ECA policy layer signals what changes next. Slovenian-language material is essentially absent at this level, so sl-language monitoring for this cell has to route through Banka Slovenije's relays of ECB studies.
